ai.literal: Shade and water are harmful if they cause harm; also the nature of relations will become harmful if they do harm.
ai.translation: Even shade and water, though normally pleasant, are harmful if they cause illness; likewise, even the relationship of one's own kin becomes harmful if they act to cause harm.
ai.modern: நிழலும் நீரும் உடலுக்கு நோய் போன்ற துன்பத்தைத் தருமானால் அவை தீமையானவையே; அதுபோல, நம் உறவினர்களின் தன்மையும் நமக்குத் துன்பம் தருவதாக இருந்தால் அது தீமையானதாகவே முடியும்.
ai.explanation: The poet uses a beautiful analogy from nature to explain internal enmity. Shade and water are universally sought after for comfort, yet if they cause sickness, they are avoided as harmful. Similarly, one's own relatives and close associates are expected to offer support and comfort. However, if their character and actions bring harm or betrayal, that relationship becomes toxic and must be treated as dangerous. The word 'நீர்' is brilliantly used twice with different meanings: first as 'water' (paired with shade) and second as 'nature or character' (of relatives).

ai.literal: Sword-like enemies do not fear; fear friend-like enemies' alliance.
ai.translation: Do not fear enemies who are like an open sword; fear the alliance of enemies who pretend to be friends.
ai.modern: வாளைப் போல வெளிப்படையாக இருக்கும் பகைவர்களுக்கு அஞ்ச வேண்டாம்; உறவினரைப் போல நடித்துப் பழகும் பகைவர்களின் நட்புக்கு அஞ்ச வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts open hostility with hidden enmity. An open enemy is compared to a sword, which is visibly dangerous but straightforward, meaning one can prepare for the threat and therefore need not fear it. In contrast, one must deeply fear the alliance of enemies who pretend to be close friends or relatives. This hidden enmity is far more destructive because it operates under the guise of friendship, catching one completely off guard.

ai.literal: Fearing internal enmity, protect oneself; at the time of weakness, like the enemy of clay, it will destroy completely.
ai.translation: One must fear internal enmity and guard oneself against it; otherwise, at a moment of weakness, it will destroy one completely, just as a tool cuts through clay.
ai.modern: உட்பகைக்கு அஞ்சி ஒருவன் தன்னைத் தற்காத்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்; இல்லையெனில், தளர்ச்சி ஏற்படும் காலத்தில், அது மண்ணை அறுக்கும் கருவியைப் போல அவனை முற்றிலும் அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the extreme danger of internal enmity, which refers to hostility from those within one's own circle. The poet advises that one must fear and guard against such hidden enemies constantly. If left unchecked, at the first sign of vulnerability or distress, this internal enemy will destroy a person completely. The destruction is compared to the tool that cuts clay, which slices through soft clay effortlessly and decisively.

ai.literal: If internal enmity of an unfitting mind arises, it will bring many ruins that make one's kin discordant.
ai.translation: If internal enmity arises from an insincere mind, it will bring many ruins that destroy the unity of one's kinsmen.
ai.modern: மனம் ஒன்றாத உட்பகை ஒருவனுக்குள் தோன்றினால், அது அவனுடைய சுற்றத்தாரைப் பிரிக்கும் பல துன்பங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the severe dangers of hidden, internal hatred. When internal enmity arises from a discordant or insincere mind, it does not remain a quiet grudge. It actively works to divide and ruin one's own group or kinsmen. Ultimately, this internal division brings about numerous forms of disaster and ruin to the entire household or community.

ai.literal: If internal enmity arises by way of relationship, it will bring many afflictions by way of ruin.
ai.translation: If internal enmity arises among those who are closely related, it will bring many fatal afflictions that lead to utter ruin.
ai.modern: உறவினர் போன்ற நெருங்கிய முறையில் உட்பகை உண்டானால், அது அழிவை உண்டாக்கும் வழியில் பல துன்பங்களைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the extreme danger of secret hatred arising among close associates or relatives. The word 'uṟal-muṟaiyāṉ' refers to the manner of close relationship, indicating that the enemy is disguised as a close ally. The word 'iṟal-muṟaiyāṉ' mirrors this structure, meaning 'by way of ruin or death'. The poet emphasizes that when hatred develops within one's own circle, it does not just cause minor setbacks; instead, it systematically delivers numerous fatal afflictions that inevitably lead to complete destruction.

ai.literal: If discord arises among those who are united, at any time, not perishing is difficult to happen.
ai.translation: If discord arises among those who are closely united, it is impossible for them to escape ruin at any time.
ai.modern: நெருங்கிய நண்பர்களுக்கிடையே அல்லது உறவினர்களுக்கிடையே மனவேறுபாடு ஏற்பட்டால், அவர்கள் அழிவிலிருந்து தப்பிப்பது எக்காலத்திலும் இயலாததாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the severe danger of internal division among close allies. The word 'onṟāmai' refers to discord or lack of unity, while 'onṟiyār' refers to those who are closely united. If such discord arises ('paṭiṉ') within a united group, escaping destruction ('poṉṟāmai') becomes impossible ('aritu') at any point in time ('eññāṉṟum'). The poet emphasizes that internal enmity is so destructive that survival is completely ruled out once unity is broken.

ai.literal: Like the joining of a metal box, even if they join, they will not truly unite, the family beset with internal enmity.
ai.translation: Even if they seem to fit together closely like the lid and a casket, a family beset with internal enmity will never truly unite.
ai.modern: உட்பகை கொண்ட குடும்பத்தினர், செப்பின் மூடியும் உடலும் பொருந்துவது போல வெளியில் கூடி வாழ்ந்தாலும், மனதால் ஒருபோதும் ஒன்றாக இணைய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the vivid metaphor of a metal box (செப்பு) and its lid. Although the lid and the box fit together so perfectly that they appear to be a single unit from the outside, they remain two separate pieces that never actually fuse. Similarly, members of a family (குடி) who harbor internal hatred (உட்பகை) may live together and appear united to the world, but their hearts and minds remain completely divided and can never truly bond.

ai.literal: Like metal rubbed by a file, will wear away, strength being worn down, the family that has suffered internal enmity.
ai.translation: Like metal filed away by a rasp, a family that harbors internal enmity will gradually wear away, losing all its strength.
ai.modern: அரத்தினால் தேய்க்கப்பட்ட இரும்பு தேய்ந்து போவது போல, உட்பகையைக் கொண்ட குடும்பமானது தன் வலிமை அழிந்து மெல்ல மெல்லத் தேய்ந்து போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid physical analogy to describe the destructive nature of internal hatred. The word 'அரம்' refers to a file or rasp, and 'பொன்' here denotes metal, which is normally hard and durable. Just as a file slowly but surely grinds down even the strongest metal, internal enmity ('உட்பகை') silently eats away at the core strength ('உரம்') of a family or clan ('குடி'). The destruction is not sudden or loud, but a gradual, inevitable wearing away until nothing remains.

ai.literal: Like a split fraction of a sesame seed, even though it is of such small measure, if internal enmity exists, ruin will happen.
ai.translation: Even if it is as minuscule as a split sesame seed, if internal enmity exists within, ruin is certain to follow.
ai.modern: எள்ளின் பிளவைப் போன்ற மிகச் சிறிய அளவு உடையதாக இருந்தாலும், ஒருவரிடம் உட்பகை இருக்குமானால் அழிவு நிச்சயம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the devastating power of internal discord. The poet uses the metaphor of a split sesame seed ('எட்பகவு') to represent the smallest possible unit of division. Even if the internal enmity is as tiny and seemingly insignificant as this fraction, its mere presence ('உள்ளது') guarantees complete ruin ('கேடு'). The lesson is that internal division, no matter how small, must never be tolerated as it inevitably leads to destruction.

ai.literal: Agreement those-who-do-not-have life small-hut inside snake-with together dwelling is-like.
ai.translation: Living with those who have no inner harmony is like dwelling together with a snake inside a small hut.
ai.modern: மன ஒற்றுமை இல்லாதவர்களுடன் கூடி வாழும் வாழ்க்கை, ஒரு சிறிய குடிலுக்குள் பாம்போடு சேர்ந்து வாழ்வதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the extreme danger of internal enmity or living with people who lack genuine agreement and harmony. The poet compares this situation to living inside a tiny, confined hut (kuṭaṅkar) with a venomous snake (pāmpu). In such a small space, there is no escape, and one is in constant, mortal danger of a sudden, fatal bite. Similarly, living with insincere people who harbor secret enmity means living in perpetual, unavoidable peril.
